title: Procurement intake / contract risk triage with Enterprise Ops
summary: Initial procurement intake and contract triage: reviewed MSA/DPA hotspots, SLA credit language, onboarding steps for PO and vendor portal, security artifacts requested (SOC 2, DPA, SSO details, KMS options). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share redline MSA and SOC2 pack, customer to share procurement checklist and procurement committee timeline.
next_steps: Redwood to send draft redline of MSA + DPA within 2 business days
Redwood to attach SOC 2 type II report and latest penetration test summary
Customer to upload procurement checklist to shared workspace and confirm PO lead by 2025-11-10
Schedule follow-up sync with finance/procurement on 2025-11-12 if checklist complete
action_items: Jordan Alvarez: circulate redlined MSA and DPA to Nina and Leah by 2025-11-05
Priya Shah: export short security pack (SOC2 summary + pen test high-level) and post link by 2025-11-05
Nina Patel: flag any mandatory indemnity or term changes by 2025-11-07

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-03 16:00 UTC | Duration 47m | Attendees: Jordan Alvarez, Priya Shah, Mason Lee (Redwood) — Leah Carter, Omar Rodriguez, Nina Patel, Jason Wu, Asha Menon (Summit Financial)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and we'll get right into the procurement questions and any contract hotspots.
[00:12] Leah: Thanks, Jordan. We're coming in with a fairly standard procurement intake. Procurement committee wants to understand the MSA exceptions, DPA terms, and SLA credit mechanics. Also timeline — we have a pricing approval window next week.
[00:25] Jordan: Got it. Priya and Mason are here for tech and legal. Priya, do you want to run through any deployment constraints that might affect the DPA?
[00:33] Priya: Sure, hi. Two things I want to highlight up front — we support hosted API, dedicated pools, and private VPC on-prem options. For regulated customers like you, we usually recommend either Dedicated or Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC, that way sensitive data stays in your network.
[00:49] Omar: Right — our security folk will push for VPC or on-prem. We also need to confirm KMS integration and key rotation details. Is HSM/KMS supported?
[00:57] Priya: We integrate with cloud KMS providers and can do customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. There's a configuration doc we'll share. For hosted, we offer encryption at rest with our keys but can negotiate bring-your-own-key for enterprise plans.
[01:12] Nina: On the legal side, a few standard asks: mutual indemnity, limitation of liability caps — we're averse to high service credits as sole remedy — and termination-for-convenience notice period. Also DPA should have clear data export and deletion commitments for EU data subjects.
[01:26] Mason: Noted. On liability caps, we have standard enterprise terms we can propose; some customers request carve-outs for gross negligence or willful misconduct. For SLA credits, we typically provide service credits tied to downtime buckets. We can walk through the SLA tables — are you looking for a specific uptime number?
[01:41] Jason: Ideally 99.95 for prod. We understand cost tradeoffs. Also need RTO/RPO expectations for critical services — how quickly can you failover or move to a warm pool?
[01:53] Priya: Our Dedicated offering targets p95 latency SLAs and 99.9–99.99 uptime depending on committed capacity. For 99.95 you usually want reserved capacity plus cross-region failover; we can document the recommended architecture. Warm pool failover times depend on model and KV cache warm-up; typical plan is 5–15 minutes for a configured warm standby.
[02:12] Leah: OK that's helpful. Procurement wants to know invoice cadence: do you accept Net30 and do you require a signed PO in advance? And are there any onboarding fees?
[02:21] Jordan: We accept Net30 for enterprise contracts; sign-off via PO is fine. There may be a one-time onboarding fee for Private deployments due to setup labor — we'll call that out. We can be flexible on payment terms for multi-year or committed capacity deals.
[02:36] Asha: For accounting, we need a supplier onboarding packet and W-9 (US) or equivalent tax forms. Also vendor risk questionnaire — we use a third-party portal for docs upload. Can Redwood integrate?
[02:46] Jordan: Yes, we can upload to customer portals; we often provision a vendor packet including SOC 2, ISO summary, org chart, insurance cert. Priya will attach the pack.
[02:55] Omar: On privacy — DPA: specifically subprocessors list and ability to audit. We might ask for a subprocessor list and a standard DPA addendum. Also retention: 30–90 day options?
[03:06] Priya: Subprocessor list available; we maintain an up-to-date registry. Retention defaults are 30 days for transient logs and 90 days for request traces, but we can negotiate retention windows on enterprise plans and private deployments. Deletion calls are supported; we have procedures and audit logs.
[03:21] Nina: On indemnities, we usually demand IP carve-outs and a carve-out for third-party claims if customers provide prompts containing third-party content. How do you handle IP claims?
[03:30] Mason: We follow the usual approach — indemnity for breaches of Redwood's obligations and IP infringement tied to the model service. For prompt-contained IP disputes, it's more complicated; we can add contractual language that clarifies responsibilities. I'll have legal review examples.
[03:44] Jason: Another thing — SSO and RBAC. We need SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Auditing hooks into our SIEM. Can you provide logs to Splunk/Datadog?
[03:55] Priya: Yes, SAML, SCIM, and audit export are supported on enterprise tiers. We can stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3. We'll include the integration guide.
[04:08] Leah: Great. Procurement also flagged change-of-control and assignment language — they're strict on automatic assignment to third parties.
[04:15] Mason: We can look at tailored assignment clauses; many customers add notice and consent controls. I'll surface typical compromise language.
[04:22] Leah: About the timeline — procurement committee meets next Tuesday, 2025-11-11. They want to see the redlined MSA and an exec summary of security within three business days to decide whether to advance to pricing approval. Can you meet that?
[04:34] Jordan: Yes, that's reasonable. We'll prioritize a redline and a 1-2 page security exec summary. Priya, Mason — can you get those out in two business days?
[04:42] Priya: Yes — I'll bundle SOC2 summary, pen test high-level findings, and the syslog/SIEM integration note.
[04:47] Mason: I'll do the MSA redline and flag non-starters; if there's anything unusual from your side Nina, ping me.
[04:54] Nina: One ask — we sometimes require higher insurance limits. Do you carry E&O and cyber insurance?
[05:00] Jordan: We have cyber and E&O; we'll include a certificate of insurance in the vendor packet.
[05:05] Asha: For PO acceptance, is an electronic signature on the MSA sufficient or do we need a counter-signed paper copy?
[05:13] Jordan: eSignature is fine; we accept DocuSign signed MSAs and then a PO for billing is normal.
[05:20] Leah: OK, last big procurement question — commercial approval: any required approvals from pricing committee? We need to know if the deal requires exec sign-off if discounts exceed X percent.
[05:29] Jordan: Usually discounts beyond standard tiering go to a pricing committee; we'll surface any non-standard discount in the quote and flag whether executive approval is needed. It helps if you can share target ARR or committed capacity so we can propose a structured rebate/commitment.
[05:40] Jason: On technical procurement, we might ask Redwood to run a short bench test — a supply chain performance test — to validate latency from our primary region. Is Redwood open to a brief benchmark?
[05:50] Priya: Absolutely. We can run a targeted latency and throughput test against a safe model variant; we can coordinate test windows and an SE-led script. For hosted evaluation we'd recommend small scale calls; for dedicated we'll run from the target region.
[06:04] Omar: We need to ensure that any benchmark won't leak PII — tests will use synthetic prompts.
[06:09] Priya: Understood. We'll provide a test script and a scrubbed dataset.
[06:14] Leah: Procurement also wants an onboarding timeline estimate — from PO to production how long for Dedicated vs Private?
[06:20] Priya: Dedicated: typically 2–4 weeks depending on capacity; Private (VPC/on-prem) can be 4–8 weeks due to network setup and KMS. Onboarding includes config, SSO, audit log hookup, and model provisioning.
[06:34] Nina: Regarding DPA termination clauses, do you support data return and certified deletion on termination?
[06:40] Mason: Yes, we include data return/export and certified deletion procedures and a timeline — typically 30 days for exports and 90 days for long-tail retention unless you require sooner. We'll add a firm SLA for certified deletion in the addendum.
[06:55] Asha: Will the invoicing show monthly metered usage and any overage charge lines?
[07:01] Jordan: Yes, invoices itemize committed fees, metered usage, and line items for overages and addons. We'll provide sample invoice for your finance review.
[07:09] Leah: Ok, to recap, we need: redlined MSA + DPA, SOC2/pen-test pack, sample invoice, vendor packet, and proposed SLA table scoped for 99.95 target.
[07:21] Jordan: Correct. We'll aim for 48–72 hours on that. One more thing — do you have any non-negotiable procurement clauses?
[07:28] Nina: Data residency restrictions for EU data, stronger indemnity language for consumer PII incidents, and audit rights are the top three.
[07:36] Mason: All right, we'll flag those items and propose compromise language where appropriate.
[07:41] Jason: If you can also include an architecture diagram for dedicated with cross-region failover that'd be helpful for our ops team.
[07:48] Priya: Will do — I'll attach a recommended architecture and a model on warm standby.
[07:54] Jordan: Great. Any final Qs?
[08:00] Leah: No, that's it. We'll expect the documents and timeline. Thanks everyone.
[08:06] Jordan: Thanks all — we will follow up via the shared workspace and schedule the finance sync for 2025-11-12 tentatively.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "redline" sometimes transcribed as "red light" in the auto export) and speaker label swaps observed in some segments.

References shared during call: link: https://redwood.example.com/vendor-packet (SOC2 + insurance cert placeholder), link: https://drive.example.com/summit-procurement-checklist (customer portal reference)

End transcript.
